format: BlockState.updateShape answers (vanilla 26.3). A case puts subject state S at the centre cell with the given neighbour states, air everywhere else (light 15), and calls S.updateShape toward each direction in direction_order with the state found there, replacing S with the answer as it goes, pass after pass until a pass changes nothing (at most 3 passes); the recorded result is that settled state. Neighbours are never updated. Every state id is a vanilla global state id (Block.getId, as in block_states.json; 0 = air). Subjects are the imported blocks by class: StairBlock, FenceBlock, WallBlock, FenceGateBlock, IronBarsBlock (panes and bars). Compact groups {"r":{"<result id>":[[first,last],...]},"m":[[first,last],...]} map each result to the runs of consecutive neighbour state ids that produce it (every id in a run was tested); m lists the neighbour ids whose case needed more than one pass. single_neighbour: per representative, its default state with one neighbour (air or any imported state) per direction, groups per direction. cross_family: per subject block, its default state with one neighbour from samples per horizontal direction, groups per direction. wall_up rows: [sides, above, result, one_pass]: cobblestone_wall default with stone at the listed sides and above at the cell above. stairs.single: per straight dry oak_stairs state, one oak_stairs or cobblestone_stairs neighbour per horizontal direction, groups. stairs.pairs rows: [subject, main_dir, main, side_dir, side, result, one_pass]: a straight dry same-half oak stair at the subject's facing side or its opposite (main) plus one at a side perpendicular to the facing. gates_in_wall rows: [subject, sides, neighbour, result, one_pass]: a closed oak_fence_gate state with the neighbour state at the listed sides.
